file: papers/pdf/Grimes - 2018 - The Pivot - How Founders Respond to Feedback through Idea and Identity Work.pdf
read_by: Claude Opus 5.5 in a Claude Code session (not the API), 21 Oct 2026; Kirtley and Shah replies corrected after reading the cited passages in full
about: How entrepreneurs who feel strong ownership of their ideas respond to critical feedback, and how they either hold on to, sharpen or pivot away from the original idea.

candidates.label: Pivot after outside feedback
candidates.definition: Feedback from others leads the founder to change the idea itself, abandoning part of the original concept for a new direction.
candidates.applies_when: The founder says outside feedback made them drop or substantially change the original idea.
candidates.does_not_apply_when: Feedback only refined the wording or framing while the founder kept the core idea; that is sharpening, not pivoting.

candidates.label: Feedback that sharpens the idea
candidates.definition: Critical feedback prompts the founder to restate the idea more clearly around what they care about, keeping its core.
candidates.applies_when: The founder describes feedback that made them clarify what the idea is really about without abandoning it.
candidates.does_not_apply_when: The feedback led to a different idea altogether (a pivot).

candidates.label: Psychological ownership of the idea
candidates.definition: The more founders feel the idea is theirs, the more they resist feedback that would change it.
candidates.applies_when: The founder describes the idea as personally theirs and pushes back on suggested changes.

candidates.label: Abstracting the idea to its core
candidates.definition: Founders respond to criticism by moving the idea to a more abstract level so that the core survives while details change.
candidates.applies_when: The founder restates the idea at a higher level (the purpose or need) after criticism of specifics.

candidates.label: Treating ideas as hypotheses to test
candidates.definition: Some founders treat their idea as a hypothesis that feedback can confirm or refute.
candidates.applies_when: The founder describes testing the idea and being willing to change it on the evidence.

candidates.label: Collective sensemaking with others
candidates.definition: Working through feedback with co-founders or others shapes whether and how the idea changes.
candidates.applies_when: The founder describes interpreting feedback together with others before deciding what to change.

candidates.label: Breadth of prior experience
candidates.definition: Founders with broader experience across domains respond differently to feedback on their idea.
candidates.applies_when: The founder draws on varied past work or domains when deciding how to respond to feedback.

candidates.label: Visionary versus scientist self-image
candidates.definition: Founders narrate themselves either as visionaries who hold to the idea or as scientists who test it.
candidates.applies_when: The founder describes their stance toward the idea as visionary conviction or as experimental testing.

candidates.label: Deliberate lean testing
candidates.definition: Changes to the idea can come from deliberate, planned testing with customers rather than from unexpected input.
candidates.applies_when: The change followed a planned test or experiment the founder set up on purpose.
candidates.does_not_apply_when: The input that changed the idea was unsought or unexpected.

candidates.label: Idea described as sparked or born
candidates.definition: Founders describe the origin of their idea as a spark or birth, a sudden moment rather than a search.
candidates.applies_when: The founder narrates the idea as sparked, born or arriving at a moment.
